28 A light wave passes through a single slit and a diffraction pattern forms.
What happens to the frequency and the speed of the wave when it is diffracted?
frequency
speed
A
decreases
increases
B
increases
decreases
C
no change
decreases
D
no change
no change

hints: Notice the light before and after the single slit travels in the same medium - only its spreading to form the diffraction pattern is new.
Recall that frequency $f$ is fixed by the source and wave speed $v$ is fixed by the medium, linked by $v = f\lambda$.
Ask whether spreading of the wave at the slit requires $f$ or $v$ to change if neither the source nor the medium has changed.
walkthrough: Identify the situation: a light wave meets a single slit and spreads, but the incident and diffracted light are in the same medium.
State the rule for frequency: $f$ is determined by the source of the wave, and passing through a gap does not create a new source.
State the rule for speed: for light in a given medium $v$ is determined by that medium, so with no change of medium $v$ stays constant.
Use $v = f\lambda$ to check consistency: with $v$ and $f$ fixed, wavelength $\lambda$ is also fixed, and diffraction only redistributes amplitude with angle.
Therefore frequency shows no change and speed shows no change. This is option D.

A.explanation: Diffraction through the slit does not lower $f$ or raise $v$; both are fixed by the source and the medium.

B.explanation: Spreading at the slit does not create a higher frequency or a slower wave when the medium is unchanged.

C.explanation: Frequency is unchanged, but speed is also unchanged because the light remains in the same medium.

D.explanation: Diffraction only changes direction and amplitude distribution, so $f$ set by the source and $v$ set by the medium both stay the same.
